distinguishing_features: Embeds conductive epoxy equipotential interlayers inside the bushing potting rather than monitoring leakage-current or tan-delta signatures.
Segments the radial insulation into voltage-graded dielectric sections with layer radii selected from a voltage-division calculation.
Uses manufacturing injections and ultrasonic QC to implement and verify the physical grading structure without new sensors.
Uses measured surface field-gradient reduction at the conductor interface as the acceptance criterion.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce local electric-field enhancement at the conductor/dielectric interface of contaminated HVDC bushings to suppress tracking, film formation, and insulation degradation.
parsed.viable_reason: The proposal is not viable as written because DC division is governed by conductivity rather than the stated permittivity relation, floating high-conductivity shells do not by themselves impose equal voltage drops, and the worked example is off by a factor of ten (about 11.6 kV/mm, not 1.16 kV/mm).
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Conductive or equipotential grading screens and resistive stress-grading layers are conventional HV insulation tools, so applying them to a bushing with routine layer placement would be obvious once peak radial field is identified as the problem.
